title: Officer's trial is adjourned
article: The trial that was to look into the police cruiser crash that killed a Tagish woman has been adjourned.
Scheduled to start next Tuesday, the charges against Const. Jeff Monkman, 29, won't be heard until Dec. 6.

The territorial Crown and the defence brought the case forward this morning to reschedule it, as they agreed more time was needed. Previously set for three or four days, the trial is now expected to last five.
Monkman was charged last March with a Motor Vehicles Act offence of driving without due care and attention, a little more than five months after the crash.
After the Yukon RCMP conducted its investigation, an Outside Mountie reviewed the case as well.
Monkman was one of three RCMP officers stationed at the Carcross RCMP detachment on Sept. 27, 2003, when the police cruiser he was driving flipped and crashed at about 5:45 a.m.
The constable was uninjured, but 37-year-old Heather Lynn Benson died at the scene along the South Klondike Highway.
Monkman, a constable with six years' service under his gun belt at the time, was transporting her to Whitehorse for a court appearance after the Tagish woman was arrested earlier that night.
Benson was handcuffed with her hands in front of her at the time, and she wasn't wearing a seat-belt.
A coroner's inquest has yet to be scheduled but will be held following the conclusion of the constable's charges. In-custody deaths are routinely the subject of inquests.
Once he was cleared for duty, Monkman was reassigned as a uniformed general duty officer in Whitehorse.
